objective: Coordinator's go-ahead (18 November 2026) on BOND-METRIC-20261118-001's direction 2: where is not-all-equal bond distance a true distance? Aim for a condition on how the knots meet, proved if possible, and say whether tonight's grown bases (lines, two-order grids) satisfy it. Found while designing: on every complement-closed base (all not-all-equal and betweenness knots, any arity), bond distance minus one adds across a distinction that separates the knots, so bond distance is a metric exactly when it is one on every block of the knots; rings of knots are metric; split bases (the grown lines and grids) have bond distance at most two everywhere. Serves G1 and G16; tests A97 and A39; B200.
stop_rule: One frozen computation with its read-out; proof; referee hand-off; report.
title: Where not-all-equal bond distance is a distance
